reviewText: My 4 year old is an enduring Thomas the Tank Engine fan, but his second love has been the Disney animated series "Jake and the Neverland Pirates" which is based in Peter Pan's Neverland (and Peter Pan guests in a couple of episodes).  The only problem was that they only had one season for a long time, and he grew tired of it after frequent re-watches.  However, recently there have been quite a few new episodes featuring Jake, Izzy, Cubby, Skully, Captain Hook, Smee, Sharky, and Bones that he has absolutely loved.  My toddler likes it for the music, which is very upbeat and fun.So you can guess how ecstatic my 4 year old was when he opened the Amazon box and found...BUCKY!!!  I couldn't get the ties off the back of the packaging fast enough to get Bucky out for him.  He played with it all night, then took Bucky, Jake, and Skully to bed.  After that, he and Bucky were inseparable, he even begged me to let him take Bucky to school.  I know that this is one toy he is going to play with for a long time.Then, at the end of the week, I was an IDIOT. I had my toddler in the bath, and my son asked if he could get in.  I told him he could once I got the little girl out.  I was so busy drying her off that I didn't realize...he took Bucky into the bath with him!!  Bucky must have been submerged a full two minutes before I plucked him out.  I touched the button that makes the sounds...nothing.  I felt so awful!We took out the 3 AA batteries that Bucky comes with and left him out to dry.  48 hours later I put the batteries in and...IT WORKS!!  I am SO RELIEVED!  I am sure that the designers of this toy anguished over whether to make the first Bucky a floating boat for the bath or a high-end toy with electronics, and I'm glad they made it a high-end toy.  There are so many responses when you push the gold doubloon button that it never seems repetitious.  There is a ship's bell sound, and lots of music and Jake talking, such as "Woohoo!" and "Set sail for pirate island!" (followed by music) and "Water cannons, go!" and "Bucky, turn right!".  It's great because my toddler loves it too.THE GOOD- Lots of different, fun inspiring voices and sounds from the TV series- Jake and Skully to play with on the ship, both have slots on the bottom so you can perch them around the ship where there are pegs- NEARLY INDESTRUCTIBLE!!  Bucky has been dropped, wrestled over, and submerged, and everything still works great and no broken parts!- Interactive features: three gold doubloon buttons: one for sound, one to launch the missles, and one to open the port with Tick Tock the crocodile.- Comes with 3 missles, which have a large rounded front and launch with enough force to be fun but not enough to hurt anyone caught in the crosshairs- Has rollers on the bottom so he can 'sail' around your house (just make sure to have the 'water - bad!' conversation!)- When rolled, Bucky rocks back and forth like he is sailing- Back door to put the characters inI don't really see any bad things - it's pricey but I think the value is there.  You can get other characters such asFisher-Price Disney's Jake and The Neverland Pirates - Jake, Izzy and Cubby Pirate Packand other pieces such asFisher-Price Disney's Jake and The Neverland Pirates - Hook's Battle Boat.  I need to getFisher-Price Disney's Jake and The Neverland Pirates - Jake, Hook and Croc Pirate Packso that my 4 year old can act out Captain Hook being devious!I have attached a video so you can see the size and hear some of the sound effects (my son uses Jake to push down on the gold doubloon).

reviewText: This toy was surprisingly more durable and well thought out than first glance gives. The parts come in bags that are organized per section. It comes with a large fold out instruction sheet that is very easy to follow despite the multi-levels and uncommon methods of support that requires a wall for it to be built on. Assembling the play set was a lot of the fun of it. To make the fun last I would have to stress an old real estate saying: Location, Location, Location. Placed in the right place lends to its appeal and uniqueness. Be aware that there are many tiny shoes, handbags and accessories that have a tendency to end up on the floor beneath it, so I wouldn't place it in a high foot traffic area such as a hallway if possible. If that is the only type of location you have, I can say that it is pretty sturdy despite looking like it would break easily. I have bumped into our a few times and one time even knocked half of it off the wall. It went back together fine.After getting this kit you naturally want to explore the other kits that can expand upon this one. There are quite a few out there and you could build a large wall environment for play that would be very entertaining if you had the budget to do so. My son even played with it some bringing in his spiderman figurines. Overall my 5 year old daughter really likes it and plays with it more often than a lot of her other toys.4 Stars

reviewText: I'd have to say that this is a great toy for any self-respecting Elmo fan. He talks, gives hugs, sings. I was impressed that they even motorized the mouth so that it would also open and close (and his arms would move up and down) when he's talking or singing. It is absolutely adorable. Toggling the left foot will activate some pretend activity modes - astronauts, frogs, rabbits and horses. I also liked the fact that it recognizes when you're holding it upside down.The packaging wasn't overly complicated, just some string ties, really. Getting to the compartment on the back in order to insert the batteries (note: it takes 4 AA batteries which are NOT included, so be sure to have some on hand when you give this to someone) is a bit of a pain. That being said, most of them are, so I can't really complain too much about it. You will need a smaller headed Phillips screwdriver to get into the battery compartment, however.My main concerns are durability. It is listed as being suitable for 18-mos to 4 years. As I said, the arms are motorized, and while the fur is incredibly soft, I'm not sure there's enough padding to protect those arms. I'm looking forward to give this to my grandson (and may well update this review when I give it to him), however I'm concerned that he may break or other wise render inoperable the arms after some rough playing. Likewise, the battery compartment is a solid plastic section housed within the chest cavity of Elmo - again, while there is certainly really soft fur padding, I'm not sure that it was really enough as you can definitely feel the plastic casing when you hug it.Overall, it is definitely adorable and interactive, and should keep most Elmo fans happy and amused. My only concerns are how durable it will prove to be in a younger child's arms (particularly when there's a sleep mode for you to sleep with it), and how quickly the batteries will drain. So I do recommend it, albeit with the two aforementioned caveats.

reviewText: The premise is pretty simple - get a bunny to the top first. One picks a card, moves the allotted number of spaces (one or two) or twists the carrot (if a carrot card is chosen). Twisting the carrot causes holes in the hill to move, potentially plunging your bunny through the hole. It's very simple and makes a great first game for a preschooler. I would say the upper age limit on this game is about 5 or maybe 6.  My 4 year old likes it well enough. It's not her favorite, but it's a cute game for our collection. Ravensburger makes a lot of really great products, this isn't really their best. (Our family's favorite Ravensburger game isRavensburger Make N Break Junior - Children's Game.)

reviewText: Both my 3 year old nephew and my 6 year old niece enjoy playing with this toy.  The remote control is in the shape of a stop/go sign that the child holds up or down to control the truck.  The fireman in the truck spins around when it is in motion, so to make it go in another direction you have to stop and start it.  There was a bit of a learning curve until they both figured that out but now they've got it down pat.They've been using it on hardwood floors and have had no problem using it on that surface.  It's taken a header down a flight of six stairs onto a tile floor and didn't seem the worse for wear; it's also rammed into furniture often and I haven't seen any damage to it (or to the furniture). I've seen it in use often when the firetruck fleet comes out to play.  I've also seen them using the stop/go sign when they play other games; my nephew was holding it up when my niece and I were throwing a ball to one another and he wanted to cross in front of us when he was using his toy lawnmower (he specifically went and got the sign to use for that purpose).Both kids usually wind up laughing as they watching the firetruck dart around in various directions, usually chasing one or another of them (or me - lol).

They've even used it (carefully) to trace a design onto old tshirt with sharpies and they turned out really cute.This is a fun item for people who can think outside the box. reviewText: I love puzzles - when I have time for them.This was my first 3d puzzle so I didn't really know what to expect.  My 5 year old is very curious and loves to look at a 1970s globe that we have in our study.  I thought it would be educational for her to figure out where all of the countries and continents go on a globe puzzle.The puzzle is plastic and each piece is a little bit curved.  There is a plastic "dish" that comes with the puzzle to use in assembly.  Of course I don't read directions, so my wife had to point out its use.  The puzzle can be assembled by using the outside pictures, or inside numbers... we've done it both ways and both were a neat challenge.  once you have about 6 pieces together, the concave surface of the black dish allows you to uniformly press to ensure all pieces are fitting right..  The last piece isn't too hard, but you have to take care not to press in a section deeper than it should be.The puzzle comes with a metal stand that allows it to spin like a standard table top globe and it is very sturdy in that use.The only negative that I found was that the picture printing on the plastic pieces did not see to be as accurate as we see on cardboard puzzles.  Meaning that the image could jog a little, jagging lines up.  It doesn't ruin the puzzle look, but its not a defect, more a result of the manufacturing precision using this media I presume..Enjoy.. we did.

reviewText: Beat the Parents: 2+ Players (At least one adult and one child), Ages 8+, Average Play Time = 30-45 MinutesThe idea of the trivia questions being balanced for kids and adults is what attracted us to this game in the first place.  We would often play games like Trivial Pursuit, TriBond, and Know It Or Blow It, but were sometimes hard-pressed to find questions appropriate for each other's skill level.  This game takes out all of that guesswork.While the idea is sound, some of the questions were a bit...off.  Some of the questions that we posed to the kids seemed a bit difficult for them and others could have been answered by a chimpanzee.  The adult questions seemed all over the place, quizzing us on things like Disney, Lord of the Rings, The Jonas Brothers...we consider ourselves fairly intelligent people but I think that these questions could have been balanced a bit better.Despite my reservations, the game was well received by all involved.  The kids were working together to answer their questions, while Jennifer and I were answering questions the other didn't know.  I didn't know who "Fergie" was, but she didn't know what hatched from Eragon's egg...in effect, our unique interests helped compliment each other.All in all, it's a fun family friendly trivia game that our family enjoyed playing, and we all have a feeling that you would to.

reviewText: Hi! I am Erin T. and I run a website called theMomBuzz. Recently I received a LeapPad from LeapFrog to review and I am sharing my thoughts here on Amazon.The LeapPad has a great 5" screen. It is large and bright. I didn't see a way to control the brightness. The screen is larger than the Leapster Explorer Screen, which measures 3.2". The resolution for the LeapPad is 480 x 272. (The Leapster Explorer was 420 x 420.) It is a touch screen. You can use your finger or the supplied stylus. The stylus is magnetic, but it can be harnessed to the device with a supplied cord. An extra stylus is supplied in case one gets broken or lost. That has happened 3 times to us with other Leapsters - so it is great having that extra on hand.The LeapPad device is  white with green accents. There is also a violet option, which is nice for the girls. On the front of the tablet there is a power button, sound down and sound up button, and home button. There is also a large silver button that can be used like a finger control, to move a cursor up, down, left, right or explore other options.The LeapPad comes with a camera, video recorder and microphone. The camera can take 30,000 pictures and the LeapPad can record 120 minutes of video.GAMES & ACTIVITIES:The LeapPad is similar to the Leapster Explorer in what kids can do with it. They can read e-books, play learning games, enhance art and animation skills, listen to and play music, learn writing, watch videos, and do flash cards. It also has a built-in camera and video recorder, while that requires an additional accessory for the Leapster Explorer.One thing I LOVE about the LeapPad is that it works with other Leapster Explorer Games and Apps! That means if I download an app for my son's Leapster Explorer, I can also upload it onto my other son's LeapPad. And the boys can also share cartridges. And with the LeapPad came a HUGE library of game cartridges and apps to choose from. Most games and apps are extra, though, not included with a LeapPad purchase.What game(s) do come with your LeapPad purchase?1. PetPad: Learn to draw letters while teaching a custom pet tricks. Keep your pet healthy and clean with feeding and washing. The Leapster Explorer also comes with PetPad, but with the LeapPad kids can use the microphone to "blow dry" their pet, they shake the device to help their pet JUMP over a pond to pop balloons and they can even tilt the device to move the pet as it follows them onto their home page. You need to connect the LeapPad to your computer to use collected points to purchase food and accessories for the pet. Don't worry - it won't die if you don't do it. But it encourages you as a parent to connect the game to the computer so you can track your child's learning progress.2. Story Studio: All About Me: The artwork, photos, writing and recordings kids create all culminate in the Story Studio experience. In the Story Studio, kids create their own book that can be uploaded to view in LeapFrog Connect or shared with friends via Facebook or e-mail.3. Art Studio: I am SO THRILLED that Art Studio was included with the LeapPad. The Leapster Explorer didn't have an included Art Program - so my boys were using the Art Studio from Mr. Pencil or Tangled to get creative. The Leapster 2 DID come with an Art Studio, so I was a little sad when I found out the Leapster Explorer didn't. And whenever a parent asked me what game to get for their new Leapster Explorer, I always said, "Mr. Pencil saves Doodleburg," because it was educational and creative. But with the included Art Studio, it gives me more options for what games we can get next. With the Art Studio the boys use stamps, shapes, pattern brushes, pencils, erasers (all virtual) to create pictures and express their creativity.4. Camera/ Video Recorder: The LeapPad has a built-in camera and video recorder. My son used it immediately to take a picture of me. And then I used it to take a picture of HIM for his profile. That's when I realized that the camera is low-res. He loves taking photos and videos, but he can tell the difference of quality. But it is good for the purpose and helps keep the cost of the product lower than if it was a higher-res camera. With the camera kids can take pictures and videos and then add fun effects.Additional games, books and videos have to be added either as an app or with a cartridge. Remember, there is a library of over 100 choices. Additional apps and games are separate reviews on theMomBuzz. Please refer to the bottom of the post to connect you to these other reviews.WHO TO BUY THIS FOR:The LeapPad is designed for children 4 to 9. I would actually feel comfortable giving this to an advanced, tech savvy 2 year old. (Parents and grandparents will know who I am talking about! So many toddlers can use a smart phone better than an adult. This is a much better alternative to giving a toddler your precious iPad.)WHY BUY IT?Why do I suggest the LeapPad for kids 2 - 6? Well, my sons have owned a Leapster since they were 2 and I feel that the educational games have helped them with their writing, science and match skills. It's a creative outlet. And it's a great way to disguise learning as fun. I know some parents purchase the Nintendo DSis and other handhelds, but we've gotten away without needing to purchase one yet - even though their cousins own those handhelds. My kids have been happy with their Leapsters and the new LeapPad as their handheld and entertainment of choice. And I prefer it to, knowing the games were designed with learning in mind.Plus, the Leapster Explorer and the LeapPad are great that you can keep challenging them with new apps, they are cross-compatible to take each other's games and the LeapPad remembers your child's progress from game-to-game and book-to-book.Finally, maybe you are trying to decide between the Leapster Explorer and the LeapPad. Both are EXCELLENT devices. I :heart: them both. But with the LeapPad you are getting the camera/video recorder built in, it has a microphone, it has a larger screen and kids will experience a new way of reading with Ultra eBooks, an interactive cinematic reading experience. (I'll post more about that this week when I review the Cars2 Ultra eBook.)MORE THAN ONE PLAYER:The LeapPad does allow for more than one person to sign-on to the game. Only one person can play at a time. But... if my oldest is in school and my youngest wants to play, I can sign-in under his name. So then the LeapPad will know that the younger brother is playing and will adjust the settings to make the games challenging enough for his level of learning.And I have to say, when I first turned this on (after my 5-year old had been playing for a few hours) I saw that he created a profile for ME. How sweet is that? He had my name, my picture and chose a nice pink background for me. :heart:RECHARGEABLE BATTERIES:I am also really excited that this is the first LeapFrog device I own that accepts rechargeable batteries. Previously all the devices stated that peak performance wouldn't occur with those batteries. But that has changed now! And trust me, your kids will be running down the batteries in the beginning as they won't want to go anywhere without the LeapPad.WHAT IT COMES WITH:When you purchase the LeapPad, it comes with a CD to get LeapFrog Connect on your computer, a USB cord and an extra stylus.WHAT YOU MAY WANT TO BUY:* LeapPad Case to keep it protected when not in use* LeapPad Gel Skin to protect it when being used* Headphones so you don't have to listen to the games when traveling or in an officeAll accessories can be found at LeapFrog.com.

reviewText: This toy is great - there are separate figures of Jake and his parrot that can "stand" on different places on the ship via a hole/peg mechanism. There are also buttons on the back of the ship that when pressed, make different Jake pirate sounds.  And a button you can push that results in an alligator popping out the side of the ship (my son kept playing with this and would laugh hysterically at it).  There are also some shooting water pieces that you can slip into the front of the ship and when you press a button, go flying forward which is great for imaginary play.  The ship itself is very nice quality and looks like a real ship.  There are wheels at the bottom to allow for easy pushing/maneuvering.  I highly recommend this toy, especially if your son likes pirates or Jake the pirate.

The board and pieces have a nice weight to them and with one exception everything feels sturdy.  That one exception is a big one though.  Key to the game, is hiding three cards in an envelope. This is a great game that requires some thought and provides loads of fun.

reviewText: The box in which Chuggington's Wooden Railway Over and Under Starter Kit is packaged boasts that the railway is made of "real wood," and includes both Wilson and Koko. Who or what is Wilson? Who or what is Koko? The trains? The ones whose faces are on the trains? I don't know and it doesn't matter. This play set, as I think it would be called, is recommended for ages "3+," but I doubt the plus is meant to include anyone in my, shall we say, "advanced" age group.I gave this to my niece's three-year-old, and though he's rather articulate for his age, he refused my request for an interview. I can only assume he likes it. I didn't play with it myself, but I will say this is a high quality item with plastic that looks and feels quite durable, and, as noted, tracks made from genuine wood. There are 22 pieces (and more can be purchased separately) with two train engines, someone or something called Vee, a Clock Tower Tunnel, a Bridge Tunnel, and track pieces. Depending on the child's skill and imagination, he/she can construct this railway in a variety of ways and have a lot of fun doing it. This is a cool toy.Highly recommended.Brian W. Fairbanks

reviewText: I bought this toy for my almost 4 year old grand son. It seems a bit too young for him, but he still liked it.  I preferred it when the Fisher Price toys had the smaller people.  This one seems more appropriate for a 18 month old to a 4 year old.  He likes it now, but I was hoping for a toy that would last him a little longer.  I suppose they increased the size of the people so that they would not be a choking hazard for the youngest toddlers.  It seems there aren't many toys from Fisher Price left for the older toddlers.  He likes it, but I don't think he'll play with it more than a year.  It's just a bit too young.Also, it didn't come with the dragons that are on the TV show.  I found them at Target for $12.99, so I bought them to go with this toy.  If you watch the Mike the Knight show on TV, you'd know that the dragons are a big part of the show and I'm sure he would have wondered why they weren't there.All of that being said, if you are getting it for a 2 year old or young 3 year old, they will probably like it long enough to be worth the purchase.About the quality:  The toy is well made and doesn't have part that would break with normal use.  There are enough different things to do to keep a toddler occupied for a while.  Some of the features really don't make sense if you don't watch the TV show. reviewText: Of all the presents my daughter got for her birthday last month, it was the Furby that got the most attention. I was surprised at first, because it was one of those toys that she'd mention now and then, not expressing a whole lot of interest in. Well, here we are almost a month and a half later, and she's playing with her Furby regularly, and always brings him along for trips. I have to admit, this IS a pretty cool toy! It's leaps and bounds ahead of the original model, and does so much more. If this were around when I was a kid, it'd easily be one of my favorite toys.For starters, the new Furby has a better body model than the original. Instead of just moving its ears up and down, this new one can move its "head" to give it more personality in its actions. Furby can dance along to music, changing how it dances to different genres. The most notable difference however, is the LED eyes. All sorts of expressions are visible in the eyes now, including some wacky icons like cows and dogs that show up depending on what the Furby is doing. The more you talk to Furby, the more English he'll pick up. After about two weeks, we noticed a big difference in how he was talking and singing. The big surprise though was seeing that there are different personalities it can have. From crazy to evil to valley girl (or is that just evil 2.0?), the new Furby is full of surprises. Different personality types come and go, and if you don't like one, you can always just reset it to go back to normal. If you've owned a Furby before, you can expect everything that made that toy fun, and much more, this time around. All the Furbish, the singing, interacting with other Furbies, going to sleep when it's not being played with...Hasbro took what was worked with the original and kept those features, only making improvements. Another big selling point is the Furby app. Download the app and you can feed the Furby all kinds of things, getting different reactions out of it.I'm keeping the details about what we like about the new Furby brief because there's still so much that's undiscovered! Just when you think you've seen everything, a new personality comes out, or it will sing along with a song that I wouldn't have expected it to. This is definitely a five star toy in the fun category, but there are just a few small things holding it back from getting 5 stars overall. First, it takes 4 AA batteries. Just like how the old Furbies sucked the life out of theirs, you can expect the new Furby to go through batteries in no time if it's played with regularly. Get rechargeables when you buy one, and you'll be set. The other problem is a minor gripe of mine, and it's that the motor sound when it opens its mouth sounds almost as loud as the original Furby's. I'm no toy designer, but aren't we past noises like this? It kind of distracts from the cute and cuddly nature of the little creature, hearing mechanical sounds from inside every time it moves. The only other problem is a temporary one- it keeps selling out! Just be patient and you'll find one on here or in stores. Honestly, I'm surprised the new Furby has managed to become nearly as popular as the first model!Any child that's interested in the Furby based on what they've seen in commercials is going to absolutely love playing with it. Furby is still cute, fun to play with, and will likely be one of those toys that your kids remember when they've grown up.

reviewText: I was so impressed with this company's customer service that I wanted to share my experience with others. In this day and age it is not often that one has an extraordinary, wonderful experience when working with a customer service department. In fact, often it seems like it's just the opposite. Graveling with the employee of a company, often getting slow, disrespectful service that leaves a sour taste in my mouth, making me question my purchase and think twice before dealing with a particular company again. I was so pleasantly surprised by my experience with "I can do that games" that I wanted to provide feedback so others would know what any outstanding company this is! We have this "Busy Town Eye Found It" game and the little sand timer that goes with the game got misplaced. I got on-line at the parent company's website (I can do that games.com) to see if replacement parts were available. I didn't see anything about replacement parts, but sent an e-mail in the contact section. I promptly received an e-mail back indicating that replacement parts were available - I just had to provide what game, part that was needed, and our shipping information. I e-mailed back the information necessary and received the replacement sand timer in 2 days! WOW!!! This company deserves the highest recommendation possible! Not only did they replace the missing part for FREE (and they didn't even charge a shipping OR handling fee!!!), but they did so quickly and without having to go through a huge arduous process! Any company that has this level of customer services deserves highest honors. For this reason I would not hesitate to purchase any of this company's  products, knowing they provide superb customer support!As for the actual game, it is fun to play! Part of the game involves searching for various items (similar to looking at an `eye spy' book). Often playing a preschool age game is a little boring for the parent. This game is actually fun to play and the instructions do focus on team work. Although, you can easily adapt and play so that there is an actual winner - by making up a few of your own rules. At our house, we like to make up different versions to play, that keeps the game interesting and more versatile.This game has some small parts, so we do have to find opportunities when our 1 year old is asleep to play, because the little magnifying glass markers are definitely choking hazards. The game board is very large, which makes it fun, but also limits where you can play - namely the floor. This means that little pieces are easily accessible to my toddler (who puts everything in his mouth)! So as I mentioned we have to find times to play when the toddler won't be able to `hijack' the little pieces. No BIG deal really, just something other parents might want to know before purchasing this game. I wouldn't let that alone deter me from purchasing this well-thought-out, unique, cute & FUN game!

reviewText: My engineer husband put this together last night for our 6 year old son.  Fortunately, you don't need to be an engineer to assemble it, it snaps together pretty easily, and the instructions seemed to be reasonably clear.  There was a bit of confusion at one point, as one of the pieces that should have been labeled with a 10 on one side and 11 on the other, actually only had the 10 on one side, but since all the other pieces had both their numbers, it was not too difficult to figure out which piece this was.  Other than that, the assembly went fine.  One piece has come undone since the initial assembly (due to rough handling by the 6 year old), but it also was easy to snap back into place.  I don't think it's durable enough to survive a major accident, like being stepped on with hard shoes, but it doesn't fall apart every time you touch it like some of the marble run tracks do.It is TINY - the nano cars are about an inch long, and I worry that we'll lose them to the cat before long.  The track is nicely compact - you can set this up and leave it, unlike larger tracks where you either have to devote a room to them or disassemble them after a play session.  This easily fits on a small section of the top of the dresser.The cars are a challenge to get going.  You have to pull them back until they click, which is how a lot of these kinds of cars work, but these are more fiddly than most.  You have to put JUST the right amount of pressure on them, not too little or too much. Maybe it's because these are so tiny?  But it took several tries and some frustration for my 6 year old to figure out how to do it, although he has mastered the skill since last night, so I can't say it's TOO difficult.  Just be aware that the easily frustrated child may need a little encouragement to get these going.Once you get them going, the cars go through a series of mini loops and then through the 'booster', which gives them a motorized boost to send the car through the larger section of loops.  It doesn't always make it - sometimes the car falls out mid-loop, but mostly, if you do it right, the car will go through one full cycle of the course.  A couple times it has gone through twice, and I think it's even done 3 times.The big drawback of this toy is that it is LOUD - the motor on the booster (which requires 2 D batteries, BTW) is really ridiculously loud for as small as that motor is.  My husband took it apart to see if he could get it to quiet down, but no luck - he says the problem is that the gears are too loose in the housing.  It's not a toy a child could play with early in the morning when others are sleeping unless you have a very large or exceptionally well sound-proofed house.However, it has been a big hit - my son played with it a couple hours last night, and has played with it all morning today, and shows no sign of tiring of it.  I think other kids who are fans of race tracks and marble run toys, who have enough patience to get used to the quirks of the cars and are not very noise sensitive, would also like this toy.
summary: It's LOUD - but he loves it!

reviewText: We received the Explorer with the camera/video attachment a few weeks ago. We have a 10 year old and a 4 year old, and this system is appropriate and interesting for both age groups. The Explorer system with the camera and video attached, is sophisticated, educational, and most of all, fun.The camera attachment plugs directly into the bottom of the Explorer module, and we used the included CD to install its software on our computer. The installation was easy and seamless. The kids were instantly able to use both the still and video cameras. The whole system is small enough to take on outings. The buttons on the game console were straight forward and easy to figure out. The 4 year old needed some assistance with how to center photos, but it didn't take her long to catch on. She was also quickly adept at using the special effects software, and she has been having a blast with it.At four, she needs assistance with PC connections, and file transfers, but, for the most part, she can use the system quite competently on her own. The ten year old intuitively knew how to work everything. The only problem we had was which kid had control of the system! That problem persists.The video and photo quality is quite good, certainly far better than what has been available in the past. It is terrific to be able to transfer the files to the computer, since the memory on the system fills up quickly, especially with videos. It is easy to transfer and delete data from the card to keep it ready to record.The Explorer system with the camera attachment is now the favorite video game/camera system in the house, and the interest is not diminishing at all.The computer interaction for parents for this system is great.The only change we have to make is to purchase the charger available for the Explorer, since we sure are running through a lot of batteries!I can't recommend this system highly enough, it is very impressive, and great fun for everyone.
summary: More than a toy, fantastic gadget for a lucky child!

reviewText: When I started playing with theLeapFrog Tag Reading Systemand the Interactive Human Body Discovery pack I was mesmerized.  Mind you, I used to use Dolch cards with children when all else failed and worked heavily withHooked on Phonics, another product that Amazon sells and one I reviewed.  Children are naturally inquisitive and want to learn, but when it becomes drudgery or ends in frustration or failure ... no thanks!LeapFrog is success at the end of small handheld Tag that encourages interactive learning.  There are online tutorials that children can access with the aid of a parent, caretaker, or teacher, but what better way to learn than independently?  Once you have the Tag, which by the way is a seamless software installation process, a bit of instruction and away we go on the way to learning.At the same time children will develop fine motor skills as they use the Tag.  For example, in the section "Your Digestive System," the child must trace a path from the mouth to the stomach (or other areas).  Once there was a cheery correction, but the Tag is patient and "waits" for a successful conclusion in the digestive journey.Children are naturally curious about anatomy and physiology, but generally in more simplistic terms. reviewText: This stringing toy can be entertaining when used to encourage storytelling.  Children unfamiliar with farm animals will need some guidance.  When I introduced this toy to some preschoolers I made up a story as I showed them how to string the objects onto the cord.  The set includes wooden farm animals, including chickens, sheep, cows, a horse, and duck.  There is also a barn and an apple tree.PROS:~Very colorful and sturdy~Objects are well sized for little hands~Easy to string the objects on the cord using the wooden dowel on the end~Objects can stand on their own so can be used without the cord to just playCONS:~Despite the farm theme, there is no farmer, which hampers the storytelling aspect~The cord is merely glued to a stopper at the end of the cord, making it highly likely it will come off.  Also, the children kept picking at the hole, trying to get the glue out.I feel that this toy succeeds best when introduced with some storytelling to ensure children know all the animals and other objects.  I was very pleased with the durability of the toy but would encourage amending the design with a better stopper on the end of the cord and adding a farmer, although it might be difficult to avoid stereotyping the farmer object.

reviewText: This is one of my daughter's favorite toys to play with at the moment. The height is perfect, there are many different phrases (and we're always finding new ones), and there is so much to do. I love the colors, they aren't boring like a lot of gender neutral toys but bright and cheery. The assembly was easy enough, although I had to take it apart when we traveled over Christmas and then put it back together from memory because I lost the manual. You can "feed" the Cookie Monter, although the plastic food only touches the black plastic that is his mouth and doesn't actually go in. There is a healthy food menu with all of the plastic foods included on it. The stove can turn from hot to cold, each setting with a comment from Cookie Monster. You can "cook" in the oven or stove top. Elmo and Abby Caddaby can be fed (the plastic food goes into their mouths and lands in the oven) and have a few phrases apiece. There are songs and a bell and basically it's a lot of fun! LOL. My daughter's favorite things to do are: feed Elmo and Abby, retrieve the "fed" food from the oven, and turn the menu back and forth. I was surprised to see that she recognized Abby Caddaby (she has and Abby toy and pj's) and tries to talk to her sometimes (so cuuute). You won't be disappointed with this one!

The tracks go together in various formations and it's easy for little hands to set up.  The packing was a bit over done - lots of little elastic bits that needed to be cut off, but little set up after that.  It does not come with batteries.  Be prepared for a little disappointment. It does read on the box that these are accessories and are not included, but your little one is going to expect them to be in the actual set.Point of View of the Almost 4-year-old:My daughter is not a girly girl when it comes to toys.  She loves cars, boats, planes, etc.  Barbie doesn't stand a chance, though she does like Barbie's dog.  Though a bit disappointed at the girly colors (she prefers red), she loved the train.  Although she liked that it came with one pony, she prefers to use it to cart around her other small animal toys.  The train is easy to turn on and off without my help and her hands handle the tracks with ease.  I spent all last night and much of this morning playing with this one with her and she shows no sign of tiring of it.  It's a winner in her book!

reviewText: Koryo is a pretty basic card game with a goal of ultimately scoring the most amount of "influence points". The game has 8 rounds with a declining number of cards dealt in each hand (10 to start and 3 at the final round). You are limited in what you can play to matching suits unless you draw a special card that permits you to play unlike cards.Again, all basic stuff. But somehow Koryo manages to make the easy complicated. It's a quick game (10 mins for 2 player) but we found for the first few times we were constantly referring to the instructions and constantly having to check how many cards we could have in front of us and if we were in line with the card rules. It would have been much better to have clearer info ON THE CARDS themselves as the symbols on the cards aren't very descriptive.The frustrating thing about Koryo is that it feels like you are constantly shuffling and dealing cards. Round after round you reshuffle the discard pile into the draw pile and in a 10 min game you do this 8 times. That's a lot for such a short game. The game play is also super clumsy. It always feels like you're playing the luck of the draw rather than a solid long term strategy and with a declining number of cards that you can draw each round your options become more and more limited.Koryo isn't a bad game, it's just not one that makes you want to play it again and again. It'll be fine as a quick filler, or to play while you're waiting for someone to be ready for a much longer or more in depth game. It just feels like it wasn't play tested enough, with some tweaks it could become a MUCH better game, as it stands... it's Just OK.***Update 7/15/2014***After playing this a few times now we've gotten more frustrated with it. Many games have come down to how good the last three cards you are dealt are, way too much reliance on "luck of the draw". I'm sure this will get permanently shelved when our copies ofJaipurandBiblios Board Gamecome.

reviewText: Our grandchildren, ages 8 and 6, loved this game because they were competitive with us and it was fast paced.  It improves dexterity and eye-hand coordination in a fun game which can level the ages when using variations to the rules.  The players race to put together a 'building' matching a building card.  We did not use the variation which can handicap the older players so they use only one hand when building. Another variation is using the easier yellow cards (up to four blocks) for younger players, and the more difficult red cards (up to six blocks) for advanced players. As always, Ravensburger games are well made and well thought out.

reviewText: This is a very fun family game, and caused the kids to laugh out loud at all of the wrong answers Mom and Dad gave, with various groans and "I can't believe it" responses from the adults at the level of ease of the kid questions.  This is one the kids will absolutely win each and every time - unless the parent is 150% involved in each minute of a kids day - and that's ok: the kids need to win, too.Overall, this is a well thought out and entertaining game: the kids are responsible for answering general knowledge questions, and the parents / adults have to answer questions relating to kids' television shows, books, and other items unique to a kid's world.  My family plays a lot of board games, and this one is now our favorite.  From an age standpoint, I would say a kid could be 5 - 15 and still enjoy it.This game takes us about 20 minutes to play each round: much better than the never-ending game of "Sorry" or "Trouble" that can get caught in an endless loop as you pieces move back to the start line. reviewText: I have an aging father that needs something to do to keep his mind occupied. We have been doing puzzles with him that he has enjoyed. I ordered this for him as I thought it would keep us busy for a longer bit of time without getting boring. The finished size should be about 27x20.  Upon opening the box he seemed overwhelmed. There are sooo many pieces and they are quite small for arthritic hands. Most of them are blue, for the water and sky, which seemed to intimidate him.The subject matter, the Portofino Harbor is beautiful, and he loves the water, but there was no fold-out of an example of the finished piece to guide you. The picture of the completed puzzle on the box is apparently in lieu of a fold out.  This will take some time to complete, which is fine. I do wish the pieces were a bit larger for ease of handling.As for quality, the pieces are well constructed and precisely cut, so I can see why fans of Ravensburger like their puzzles. They seem like they will hold up well. As a pastime for a family with kids and teens, this would be great, lets say to take to a mountain vacation home or just leave set up as an alternative to TV or "WII" type games. I think the puzzle would suit most families expectations. For aging seniors, not the best choice.

reviewText: This toy arrives with batteries and it is in Demo mode upon delivery.  Be prepared for a lot of meowing and purring when you remove this package from it's shipping box because as soon as the toy senses motion or light, the kitty begins to meow and purr and move her paws up and down.  This is VERY important to know in case you are inspecting this toy before presenting it as a gift.  My inspection of the product nearly resulted in (dare I say it) letting the cat out of the bag as the recipient for this gift could hear the meowing and came to investigate.Is this toy realistic? - Not even close.  There is a rather loud mechanical sound accompanying the movements and the meowing (which doesn't seem to stop and sounds more like a cartoon character) truly begins to get under your skin after awhile.  The movement of this toy is surprisingly primitive considering the technology that is available in robotic toys.  The pouncing seems to be more of a weird lurching movement.  Despite this, my daughter is absolutely delighted with this soft interactive toy.  She is mesmerized by the green eyes and although I think the movement and sounds are goofy and unrealistic, she cuddles and carries her new "pet" everywhere.Although I think it's an overpriced toy, my daughter is very happy with her new pet and I'm not stuck with any vet bills so I guess in the long run - this toy is incredibly cheap compared to the real thing.

reviewText: As I sit down and began to assemble the set, I was reminded of playing with the electric race car sets from the 1980s. My wife and I assembled the set and let our three children (7, 4, and 3) have at it.  Repairs to gates that fell off, tracks that separated, or the columns that raise the track were pretty constant.  There are a few small pieces that were lost within 24 hours.  The playset did provide some excellent entertainment for the kids for a few days.  As happens with most new toys, after a few days the playset got moved to the corner and there it sets.The kids loved "Tizzy Tumbles", the gray rabbit looking motorized toys.  Tizzy coos, purrs, and makes all kinds of fun noises as it zips around the track.  Personally, I found the thing kind of creepy.  The sound of the thing kind of reminded me of a possessed Gizmo from the Gremlins.  The kids loved it though so that was the important thing.As I mentioned previously, the playset is a step up from the ZhuZhu line of toys.  Assembly was not difficult, but putting 40+ tiny stickers on various parts of the playset was a bit tedious.  The various gates give kids the option to direct the Furry Friend around.  The set did provide a number of hours of entertainment for the kids.I was not impressed with the design and durability of the set. reviewText: It is easy to over-think some of these reviews.  This is a small set of Thomas the Train puzzles for very young children.  Can they be chewed up if you leave your teething infant alone with them?  Yes - don't do that.  Can they be broken or torn like any other puzzle if they are abused? My kids love it and it seems like a good value.  I would definitely recommend it if you need a ~$20 gift for a birthday party or if you know a child likes puzzles and/or Thomas the Train. reviewText: My daughter is almost 2 years old and is already very competent with technology. We try to limit her use of it and she doesn't watch any television so this seemed like the perfect compromise. It's small enough and light enough for her to hold during a long car ride. The video quality wasn't the best but better than I expected. She can easily use the touch screen and loves that her face appears in the "login" screen. But I think most of all, she loves having something to call her own, as she's going through the "mine!" phase.But for the price, I would have expected a little bit more. The apps that came with the LeapPad didn't hold her attention for very long. Fortunately there are plenty to purchase and when there is a sale or a coupon, it's not that bad. I just wasn't happy that I had to spend money on it so soon after getting it.Then, there is the battery. Or lack of one. The 4 AA batteries (that were not included, by the way) didn't last very long. I would say less than 2 weeks and she isn't allowed to play with it for more than an hour a day. We ended up having to purchase the rechargeable battery and power cord. Again, I wasn't happy about having to spend more money on the device so soon after getting it.The stylus is a minor annoyance. It isn't really necessary for the apps we use and it doesn't stay in its place. I'm tempted to cut it off. The stickers weren't necessary either. I think the LeapPad looks better as is.All this aside, once I got apps that would interest my daughter and the rechargeable battery, it has been great. She loves it, I love that she stopped asking for my iPad, and we now have something to occupy her on long car rides, after the books and crayons have lost their appeal. It's easy to use and I can see my daughter using it for many years to come.

reviewText: My husband and I played this with our 14, 11 and 6 year olds.  It was fun, but I would say this is a game for 7+ (which is what the game itself recommends).  Our six year old had fun, but the asking of yes or no questions was sometimes tough for him and he would get easily frustrated.  (of course that might just be my son, but this is our experience with the game).The game was fun, and at times we would be stumped for a question, leading to some rather silly moments and lots of laughter.  A couple questions would leave the other players confused and again lots of laughing and giggling around the table.The game itself is simple: there are plastic headbands with little clips in the front, you put the headbands around your head, pop a card (NO peeking!) in the front and go around the table asking yes or no questions of the other players.  There is a timer and if you happen to guess what you are in the allotted time you can pick another card and keep going until your time runs out.There are cards with suggested questions and that did help our younger boys.  My only issue is the price I am seeing here.  There are no electronic components in the game, and in fact the pieces consist of little more than plastic headbands, paper cards, a timer and some little plastic chips, I would NOT pay $30 for this game.While the game is a cute idea and we had fun, I wouldn't spend more than $15, anything more and it is nothing more than an overpriced trendy game of the moment.

reviewText: Jigsaw puzzles have been on the scene for hundreds of years and continue to offer an entertaining activity for children.  These well formed, sturdy, easy to handle, over-sized pieces fit together well to create a bright and engaging picture with clearly defined images.  A nice move developmentally from fitting pieces in pre-formed spaces, putting this together sharpens manual dexterity and skills such as problem solving, image continuity and logic.  It can be enjoyed alone or as part of a group activity and something that grown-ups can share in comfortably.  With Christmas shopping around the corner, this would be a great low tech, creative gift.

reviewText: My daughter saw this and was somewhat interested (she's 10) but the "gross" factor in this case was actually a turn-off. I would love to see more experiments that are a bit more gender-neutral. It seems like at the one end you get the kits to make bubble bath and nail polish; at the other end you get this kit, with a gross toilet mixer, etc. This is one of the reasons to knock off a star.Another reason is that if you are giving this as a gift, the receiver's parent is going to have to splurge on some of the ingredients, which aren't included. Many are common household objects, like baking soda and vinegar, but not everyone has a disposable diaper on hand (or wants to pay for an entire box). Batteries are also required, so if you are giving this as a gift, at least be sure to include those.With those caveats mind, there are many positives.. The instructions are amusing and easy to read. Older kids can do these experiments without a lot of supervision, aside from the possible mess/stink factor. (You will want the kids to set the experiments up in a basement or maybe in the bathroom/tub, preferably in a room with ventilation. Outdoors would be ideal.) It can be a real turn-off for kids to try science experiments that are a dud, but these do work.Bottom line: I would buy this again, but hope that they will consider more gender-neutral packaging for similar kits in the future. Girls can be scientists, too!!!
summary: Good gift for kids but seems geared toward boys; experiments do work!

reviewText: We got one for our 2 year old just before we needed to take her on a series of long trips due to a lot of family events going on. This went with us on two 8 hour car rides, five or six 1.5 - 3 hour car rides, two 90 minute plane rides, two 5 hour plane rides, and countless journeys to the supermarket and various doctor's offices, all in less than 6 months. This is one of our no fail toys. She loves this thing. It's kind of annoying that I get asked to draw a Bubble Guppy 17 times in a row, but for peace on an airplane I will happily draw as many Bubble Guppies as it takes. I just have to stop forgetting to put glasses on Nonni, because that is absolutely unacceptable.Problem is, its been played with. A lot. So the magnetic powder is all over the place and will not go back down in spite of swiping the thingy back and forth a billion times. It's also really scarred up from the pen scraping all over it. I'd like to see a more durable screen and less dust. Other than that, this is a great toy and has been a lifesaver for us while traveling.

reviewText: Though this toy is aimed at ages 4+ my 3 year old grandson has had a ball playing with it with me and his 3 year old buddy. (It only held the interest of my 5 year old granddaughter for a few minutes.)Part of the box it comes in folds out to form a 34" x 11" playing area, but whenever we play with this I lay out a huge tarp (a heavy duty canvas tarp, which is easier for sitting on than the thin plastic type of tarps sold in paint departments). The tarp insures that the flying "colorful construction compound" that Crayola calls Morphix and which though pretty different than Play Doh reminds me of it, stays in a confined area instead of landing on carpeting, etc. In addition to the illustrated cardboard play area you get 3 containers of Morphix, 4 catapults, and 3 dozen molds to be used with the Morphix. With care, all of this can be put back into the original packaging for storage between play sessions, but in many cases an adult is going to have to be the one to put everything back into the container. After having heavy containers of Morphix fall onto my sock-clad feet a few times I realized that it's wisest to open the container close to or on the floor, because the packaging design is such that once you slide the outer cover off, the Morphix containers have nothing to hold them in place and unless you're being extra careful, they will slip out.Judging by how much fun my grandson and his bud have had playing with the Create 2 Destroy Fortress Invasion Ultimate Destruction Playset, I gotta rate it 5 on the fun scale, though I think this is one of many toys that will for most users have more novelty value than staying power.

reviewText: I got this for my 7 year old daughter who loves art.  She spends a lot of time drawing and coloring and she loves stencils.  This was something different for her as she can make it one big picture in patterns.  I was a little confused as to how it worked, but I didn't mess around with it, I just gave it to her.  A few minutes later I went in to see if she had figured it out and she had!  All on her own she had completed the drawing portion of the picture and was just starting in in coloring it.  I wasn't sure how many different pictures she could do, but she came up with quite a few different ones and I ended up sitting down with her so we could come up with some together.  She found it to be a lot of fun and was busy making pictures for everyone she knows for about four days and then she started getting bored.  But really, it doesn't matter what toy it is, it's only new for so long... I think if we take it out just once in awhile it'll be interesting every time.If I were to have complaints I would say that I wish it had more of the stencils as it just comes with the one and then the tiny one you can add in.  It seems like it would make more sense to have several of them.Also it comes with paper but that only lasts so long and the paper holder thing that also holds the stencil in place is perfectly square.  So when the paper runs out I'll have to cut more to make it the right size and I don't like that idea so much.Overall it was a fun thing to use and I look forward to pulling it out when she's looking at me saying "moooom, I'm boooored".Disclosure: I received this via amazon vine for review.  All opinions expressed are my own and I was not paid or influenced in any way.

reviewText: You pick it up. You fondle it. You think "Judge Dredd's Lawgiver", or "Dirigible Captain's Sidearm".And if you check on the internet, you'll find that so many others did just that, that a whole culture has sprung up around modding the Maverick, particularly in repainting it to make it look like it came from a Steampunk/Hellboy/Judge Dredd/FPS Video Game universe.The heft is naturally a little far forward of the handle, but not overpoweringly so.It fires sucker darts or any of the other types made for the Nerf range of firearms.Thought: Are they still firearms if they work on compressed air and go "pfft" instead of "BANG!"?The loading sequence is cool, with the cylinder being swung out to the side. On some the action is so loose a gentle wrist twitch will flip the cylinder into place, but manufacturing tolerances mean that that isn't guaranteed.Unfortunately, the other thing that isn't guaranteed is the firepower. I own several Mavericks and one of them severely underperforms compared to the rest. That one is due to be pulled apart for some modding into Colonel Moran's Martian Peacekeeper before long so I don't really mind.If performance is paramount to you then I'd suggest you look instead at the uglier but more powerful Nerf Strongarm pistol, which arranges similar components as the Maverick uses into a wildly different form. The cylinder action is more traditionally revolver-like than the Maverick's too.But much like the guys on Top Gear when having tested a McLaren and a Porsche they plump for the much worse all-round Ferrari, even though I have pointed you towards a far superior weapon in the Strongarm, *this* is the one I'd want to carry and use in cosplay accessorizing because it looks so much cooler than the Strongarm.Even though it is harder to load the entire cylinder in a short time.Even though it doesn't Slamfire.Even though the range is (pretend)lethally shorter.Cool outweighs utility every time. I would normally pull off a star for the lack of uniform firepower issue but every time I look at the thing I think "five stars for form".And at around $12 it is an affordable entry into the world of Nerf artillery.
summary: Surely The Most Stylish Nerf Gun Ever

We especially like these games because we can throw them quickly into a bag when headed out the door. You could easily stash one in your glovebox as an emergency kit for bored kids.

reviewText: This really shouldn't be compared with the classic Monopoly game since all it has in common is the name, the money and the presence of hotels. It's a fairly simple card game: two players take turns playing cards from their hands that allow them to spend money building floors and rooms, collect money in rent, or do various forms of damage to your opponent. It's fast-paced and easy to pick up for young kids with reading and adding ability.A few things I didn't like: some cards tell you on the back what they are (why?), the box is kind of flimsy and the awkward shape can make it hard to stuff the game pieces back in, and with three "plays" per turn, turns can take a long time and as some have pointed out, can give a player an insurmountable lead. I think it's a better game with only 2 plays per turn. Overall, we enjoy this game for a quick time-waster.
summary: Fast and fun to play with kids, who might learn a little math

reviewText: We originally got this for a road trip as our daughter (2.5) is obsessed with stickers, but we didn't want her to stick stickers all over the car.  We weren't expecting her to love this as much as she does.  She plays with it almost everyday and it has been a "must pack" for the "quiet bag" that we take with us when we go to church or other places were she needs to be occupied, but no make much noise.  She will pull this out of a huge box of stuff and it is definitely a preference.  We have been able to re-use the stickers over and over again with no decreasing in their clinging ability.  She loves all the different options (train, planes, boats, cars, construction) and will often mix them up-today a bulldozer was on a boat.  The best thing is that if she loses  enough pieces it is cheap enough that they can easily be replaced.

reviewText: I ordered this because of the great price, and because we needed some way to store all of our 2 year old's puzzles.  I didn't see anywhere if it would hold puzzles that have the little 'handle' for the child to pick up the piece (the little plastic peg), so I just ordered it to find out if it would work.  It holds them perfectly!  We have 9 puzzles in it now (7 with pegs, 2 without) and they all fit great, with room for 3 more.  Some other reviews says it won't fit Melissa & Doug puzzles, but we have several in there, so maybe it just won't hold the very thick ones with sounds, or those with very large handles or something, but ours all fit fine.  It is neat and easy storage, so we aren't always taking out 10 puzzles, when we only want to do one.  You can't just shove them back in the rack quickly, without looking, or they could miss the slot, but having to focus and put them in slowly is great for my 2 year old to practice putting things away correctly.  He has no problem using it, and has a renewed interest in his puzzles now!

reviewText: My 4 year old loves this toy.  He received another Thomas set for his birthday, and has barely looked at that one.That being said, I have a few complaints as a parent.  He has another Take and Play track, which you can literally take and play.  It has a handle and folds up into one compact piece.  If you're looking for something easily portable, this isn't it.  Folding it up requires removing one section of track, and following a bunch of other instructions I haven't bothered to memorize.In addition, someone mentioned that the winch system uses a magnet to pull Thomas to the top.  Not in our version.  There is a plastic piece that fits over the magnet on the front of the train.  The problem is that the magnet has to be longer than average (the train that came with the set does have a longer magnet than his other trains).  There is a warning on ours that the pulley will not work with all trains.  It basically won't work with any trains except the one that came with this set because all of the other magnets are too short.  Heaven help us if this particular Thomas goes missing (which it will in about 3 days).  Having a magnet would have been a much better design.  Not sure why they changed that.

reviewText: We gave our 3-year old this Gund Elmo after a day where he earned all of his gold stars on his rewards chart (something I would have a hard time doing).  He loves Elmo, and immediately took him, finding the squeezy-spot to make him speak within seconds.  Okay, so our first mistake was giving him Elmo AT bedtime.  The next two hours were "aahhh---chooo!" "Elmo would feel better if you hold Elmo's hand" and the other three phrases.  Five short phrases (including the sneeze!) wear thin quickly.But the big news is this, and I capitalize this because it is so important:  THERE IS NO WAY TO REPLACE THE BATTERIES WHEN THEY DIE.  Elmo will fall silent permanently once the pre-installed batteries wear out.  When I looked and found no way to replace them, I went back to the Amazon page, and sure enough, even Gund says it; "parents should be aware that the Feel Better Elmo does not have an on/off switch, and there is no way to change the pre-installed battery."So here is cute Elmo, who my little boy loves from Sesame Street, and one day fairly soon, he will lose his voice.  Not that I love changing batteries on toys, but that is kind of disappointing!Also important; Elmo can't be machine washed, of course, due to the batteries that soon will be useless anyway.  His robe and the tissue box are secured tightly; you can only "surface wash."The Chinese construction of Elmo isn't bad, really, but why spend $27 or so for what amounts to a temporary version of a doll?  I like the idea of my little boy hugging Elmo when he's not feeling well and getting ready for some rest, but as a toy, and even as a stuffed animal, this version of Elmo falls short.  I can't really recommend it.
summary: Cute, at first.  Frustrating on many levels later.  Please know the batteries can't be changed!

reviewText: We already have some of the zoo talkers (bought the zoo for Christmas).I was hoping that this train would also have the built in sounds for all the animals but it only makes noises for the people when they are placed in the drivers seat. However the included animals do work in the zoo. As quiet as it is we still managed to get the koala and tiger to sound off.Initially when my daughter (2yo) opened this up we played with it for probably 3 hours straight. She loved it and it went everywhere in the house. After that initial toy buzz wore off though I still catch her playing with it and lately the Ferris wheel has become a boat, a hot air balloon, a spaceship and a house. Interestingly the engine doesn't get much playtime anymore.They both seem to be pretty sturdy for a 2 year old's usage (the Ferris wheel has even done time in the tub and is still holding up well and seemingly rust free)but I imagine a larger kid (especially a boy) could figure out how to break it pretty quickly.The amount of fun a kid gets from a toy is largely dependent on the kid obviously but I think Fisher Price has done a good job of combining 3 things most kids love into one (Animals, Trains and Carnival rides).Haven't spotted any choking hazards or dangerous bits yet and aside from your kid bashing another one (or themselves) in the face with it I'd say it's a pretty safe toy for little ones.I'd recommend it (actually already have).

reviewText: the Leapster Explorer Camera and Video Recorder is an ADD ON to the Leapster Explorer (sold separately). The attachment screws in to the bottom panel of the Leapster Explorer and turns it into a video camera/recorder that even has with photo editing/enhancement capabilities (can draw on your pictures, stretch and manipulate them and play a few basic games with the images). Because you need a screwdriver to attach/detach, this will require parental superversion. You will need to detach the accessory each time you put it away as it will not fit into the leapster carry case with the camera attached to the base. So, not super user friendly, but it's not a huge deal.The accessory is easy to screw in and once attached, you're basically ready to start snapping pictures. My only criticism of this product is that the camera pictures are not great quality - there is no flash, photos aren't super great for printing and saving... but then, it is designed more as a toy and not so much as a camera.  My son did enjoy turning his shots into silly pictures and games.My son first got his Leapster when he was 3. The Leapster Explorer is a great game for kids to grow with. There are different game cartridges for different age and skill levels and like most Leap Frog games and toys, this game can really grow with your child and hold his/her interest over time. This latest add on is no different. Would recommend for maybe 5-7 age range.Overall, we liked this camera feature in the Leapter. As a video gaming/software product, Leapster in general does seem more suited for younger kids; especially now that the Ninteondo DS has a camera included as well -- older kids will likely gravitate towards a DS like system over the Leapster.  But overall this is a fun add on, and if you already have a Leapter Explorer, it is a nice accessory without spending too much money.If you don't have a Leapster yet, and are choosing between Leapster vs something like the Nintendo DS, consider the age of your child and the kinds of games he/she is going to want to play as well as the camera features of each product. Leapster just feels more educational and kid friendly to me... but the DS system has more games, better camera, online capabilities, etc.

reviewText: I got this because I thought this would be so much fun for my daughter to play with and for us to do together as a family. The concept is a very good one. You put the ball in the top or one of the tentacles and it will roll down. Then you have to lift up each shoe to find where it might have landed. This takes 2 AA batteries, which is not included. This was kind of a surprise to me since a lot of baby toys I have gotten already had batteries in it.Once batteries are put in, the responses that this toy makes was not accurate at first. But as we played with it more, it was actually correct. You have to settings: color or numbers. And you can also press the center button for it to play music. The songs it sings is kind of cute and this toy did keep my daughter engaged for a little bit. However, I think she has gotten tired of it. It helps motor skills in terms of teaching your baby to be able to put a ball into the hole and lifting up the shoe but my daughter was more interested in the balls themselves.This is especially important if you have babies who are teething, she was constantly putting the balls in her mouth and biting down on it instead of dropping it into the toy. It worried me slightly because the size of the balls, while big enough not to be choked on, still big enough for a baby to get their mouth around.So overall, the toy was a great idea but the responses are not always accurate in the beginning and I have also noticed that if you use rechargeable batteries, it doesn't seem to last too long. After playing with it maybe 10 times or less, you could tell by the responses and songs that it was already starting to die down.
summary: Good idea and entertains baby but the execution of product is average

reviewText: This is a great action feature that has so much going for it and yet lacking at the same time.Its selling feature, of course, is its ability to shoot plastic rods using an interior motor (3 x AAA batteries NOT included).  The gun itself actually rotates and shoots the rods about 4-5 inches away with minimal force, so parents should know that this isn't likely to put any eyes out yet they should still be careful with these potential choking hazards.While that part is fun and the central power unit lights up when you press it and spouts out random phrases, this toy is curiously lacking in articulation.  Why oh why can't you move the limbs of this figure?  Granted, I understand that the gun (and the conduit and servos associated with it) may have some limitations, but why can't you at least change the leg positioning, the other arm, etc.?  It reduces the toy to a handheld device transfixed in a frozen posture which frustrated a visiting 5-year old boy who was visiting at our house.That said, the quality and workmanship of the toy is top-notch and nearly equal to the look of our $100+ statuette that we have on one of our shelves.Ultimately, it depends on what you're looking for.  If you're looking for something that sits on a shelf and looks pretty with the added cool motorized gun factor, great, and it gets 4.5 stars for that.  If you're looking for a full "action" figure, look elsewhere...I'd give it 3 stars for playability in that regard.

reviewText: Our niece has wanted one of these for awhile. Always enchanted by it at the store, it's been at the top of her wish list for awhile. She's had a much smaller version and when I saw this up for review I couldn't pass it up. The toy itself is much larger than I remembered and when opening up the box I jumped with surprise as the cat started meowing and moving. It had slipped my mind it would arrive in demo mode and luckily I was alone when I jumped out of my chair.The cat itself is cute, fluffy and I can see the appeal to younger kids. It's somewhat interactive in its movements and actions when you touch its paw, etc. The only thing that I found particularly creepy was its eyes, however I usually find eyes on toys pretty creepy so it's pretty much a given.One of the main issues I've found so far when it comes to this toy is that we only have one and our nieces tend to fight over playing with it. While I would love to have two available for them, I think for our home only one would be tolerated as the sounds do have a wearing affect after a full day of on and off play between both girls.The fact is that they love it. They couldn't be happier with it and their smiles and excitement over it were more than enough to make me love it as well.ETA:One other reviewer mentioned a HUGE plus for the toy and that it makes the kids happy without being hit with vet bills for the real thing. I have to agree with this wholeheartedly.

reviewText: The Imaginext DC Super Friends Batcave playset will entertain kids from 3 to ten. It's a large structure with different levels for lots of imaginative play. However, many of the moving parts work clunkily out of the box or else feel like they won't stand up to a lot of playtime. Many of the moving parts are triggered by red discs that turn like knobs. Each disc has a pair of footprints for you to plug any Imaginext figure into and then turn like a key. However, the fit between the disc and the figures rarely snug enough to allow little hands to trigger the reaction this way. As a result, my kids gave up on this almost immediately and began opening gates and moving the elevator manually. Plus, the batsignal usually gets stuck when retracting back into its tube, the rocket launcher rarely moves far enough into place to clear the door in front of it, and so on. So while the basic structure is sound enough, many of te smaller and moving parts disappoint. Also, the footprint of the whole set is narrow enough that it tips over frequently. A pair of extending feet would have solved this problem.On the positive side, it works with all other Imaginext lines of toys, so our Batcave gas already been attacked by pirates, knights and dinosaurs. The kids and I have a great time creating stories and playing them out with the figures (Batman and Robin are included). So, it is an excellent launch point for developing imagination.Overall, my two boys love the Batcave. I would have enthusiastically given it a higher score if only more attention would have been paid to the construction quality and functionality of the moving parts.

reviewText: I purchased these for a trip to Disney World, and they were a lot of fun. One glowstick easily around my wrist (7") and also my son and husband, who are both over 6' tall. Two glowsticks makes a nice necklace. The colors are nice and vibrant, and the glow lasts for hours. The sticks will 'crack' or activate easily, so if you are carrying them in your backpack during the day to use at night, you might find them already glowing. Even so, they were glowing until we waved goodnight to Mickey.To use, there are connectors included. Be sure to have the ends of the glowstick meet halfway inside the connector. If one end is closer to the connector's end than the other, it can easily pop out. To activate, bend it slightly along it's length. You don't have to bend it very much- that can break the plastic causing the liquid to leak out. Obviously, you need to watch small children to make sure they don't chew on them or bend them enough to break the plastic.They put out a good bit of light. Once back in the hotel room, we tossed them on the dresser and found that they lit up the room like a soft nightlight- very nice for finding your way to the bathroom without having to leave the light on.I would recommend this product as it worked well and is a very good value.

reviewText: We first got this easel about a year ago for my son's birthday.  He had just turned 2 and this simple design was low enough that it allowed him to reach most of the surfaces.  It was wonderful then.  Unfortunately, a year later, not so wonderful.The good points to this easel?  As I said, it's low enough that my 2 year old was able to use it with no problem.  The trays on each side were perfect for storing his art supplies or his paints.  He was able to have everything in easy reach.  Unlike others we never really had many problems with the chalk board.  It was faint, but it worked just the way my kids liked it, so I didn't worry about it too much.  No nails-on-the-chalkboard sound and no squeaking chalk made me a happy mom.  The paper was a little tricky to get through the guide up top so I had to help my kids each time, no matter who was using it.  That was frustrating, but it wasn't as bad as it could have been.  The clips were useful.  The whole thing was also wonderfully easy to clean.  My son got paint on the dry-erase board and it came off after drying without a problem.The down side was this didn't last our move well.  A couple of the screw caps broke.  My daughter (9) decided to show her brothers how to take the screws out, so now half of them are missing.  It's not in as bad shape as it could have been, but we're now down a shelf on one side because the screws to attach it are gone.  I have to admit, I haven't tried contacting the company for replacements yet, but the point is they didn't last well.Overall the product isn't bad, and if you catch it on a good sale, it's not a bad price either.  It's a nice little easel, and it was fine as long as it was stationary in our house.  It wasn't until we moved that we had problems with the screws breaking.  I can imagine this would be a problem for anyone who has to move it around to store it to.  It's not the sturdiest of things.  It also doesn't fold up terribly well with the paper roll on the easel as well.Personally I don't think I would buy it again, but that's because I would opt for a more expensive item with a better look to it.  It served it's purpose, taking the abuse a 2 year old would give it.  It's still in good working order, so I can't complain too much, but I would opt for something a little higher end next time.
